label: Preference-independent epistemic reason from actual force and answerability (inference)
meaning: Conditional analyst argument, attribution deferred: take the ordinary belief reason that has force at its subject's actual preference; answerability carries that force to every supplied preference alternative, so it is a preference-independent ordinary reason. Low inferential distance: answerability is a universal-conditional form of the target's invariance clause, and is stronger than needed (it covers non-ordinary considerations). The encoding can still fail: each premise fails in a finite control (goalRelative lacks answerability; forceless lacks the concession). The goal-relative account grants the concession for accuracy-aiming subjects (checked separately) and denies answerability; within this vocabulary and given the concession the dispute sits in that bridge, while the preference-independent-definition route and reflective or disjunctive goal-relative accounts remain open. Establishes neither premise.
